precepts.text: Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself. When you die, your son should be in your image. He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness unto his friends: meaning your son will look after your father's friends.
precepts.point: King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died., you came in to collect money? We ain't giving you nothing. And Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot to flee to Jerusalem; he said, they going to kill me next. So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Rehoboam took his father’s throne. “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” When you die, your son should be in your image. “While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.”

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.” Your son is supposed to look after his father’s friends.

The old men who stood before Solomon were his father’s friends, and they counselled him: “If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.” “But he forsook the counsel of the old men”. And he was like his father in the worst way: Solomon in his old age forced the people to pay tribute to the houses of his wives’ gods, and Rehoboam said, “my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” I am going to be worse than my father.

precepts.text: Not a novice: a novice means a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte. Lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil: I know all the precepts. His head gets big cuz he thinks he knows it all. That's young men, and this type of spirit will destroy himself. So that's who Rehoboam looked to. Some of y'all in here make that same mistake.
precepts.point: King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died., you came in to collect money? We ain't giving you nothing. And Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot to flee to Jerusalem; he said, they going to kill me next. So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Rehoboam “forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him”. Those are his peers. Notice the difference: to the old men he asked, “How do ye advise that I may answer this people?” To the young men, “What counsel give ye that we may answer this people”? We, all together: y’all are my peers, we are running this thing.

Paul warns about that kind of counsel: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” A novice is a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte. Lifted up with pride: I know all the precepts. His head gets big because he thinks he knows it all. That is young men, and that type of spirit will destroy itself.

So that is who Rehoboam looked to, and the young men told him to say, “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.” Some of you in here make that same mistake.

We just had a case like that in Cali; we have many cases in the states, New York, Texas, where brothers felt, in order to be a leader of the sanctuary, I got to rule the people with roughness and pride, and they was taking advantage of the brothers and sisters out there. note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel”. Sirach tells what that does: “The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.” You rule people with roughness and pride, you are going to lose your position.

That is what happened to Rehoboam. The ten tribes said “What portion have we in David?” “to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” When he sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, all Israel stoned him to death: you came to collect money? We are not giving you anything. Rehoboam made speed to get up to his chariot and flee to Jerusalem, thinking they would kill him next. “So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.”

We just had a case like that in Cali, and many cases in the states, New York and Texas, where brothers felt that in order to be the leader of the sanctuary they had to rule the people with roughness and pride, and they were taking advantage of the brothers and sisters. No: we had to remove you. Roughness and pride is the losing of authority.

He made priests of the lowest of the people, and ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, devised of his own heart, in place of the feast of tabernacles. That is the shame of Bethel. Images shown in class: the horned gods of Chinese religion, carved with the cow's head and body, very similar to Baal, the calf god. More proof of who they are.
precepts.point: And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth–el their confidence.” Chemosh was their god; Moab always had a lot of gods, but Chemosh was the favorite. Notice it says the house of Israel, the northern kingdom, was ashamed of Bethel. What is it talking about?

“Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” Two calves, and our people were worshipping them. “And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.”

“And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.” Then “Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah”. Judah kept the feast of tabernacles on the fifteenth day of the seventh month; Jeroboam and the northern kingdom said, we are going to do the eighth month, the fifteenth day, “even in the month which he had devised of his own heart”, sacrificing unto the calves in Bethel. That is the shame of Bethel: calves of gold, false priests and a feast made up in his own heart.

Moab will be ashamed of its gods the same way. Look at the gods in China today: horned gods, very similar to Baal, the calf god, carved in stone with the cow’s head and body. Israel had two calves; these gods have the same horns. More proof of who they are. And just as Israel was brought to shame for Bethel, Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Notice this: even before the split of the kingdom, the tribes that would become the northern kingdom were already dabbling with Baal. Gideon's own father had an “altar of Baal” and a grove by it, worshipping the Lord in some fashion while holding onto the idol, and the men of the city worshipped it too, which is why Gideon had to throw it down by night.

That is why it was such an easy transition when Jeroboam “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” The north had been dealing with Baal long before the split ever happened; Jeroboam only gave them what they were already used to.

precepts.text: Jeroboam's fear: if this people go up to sacrifice at Jerusalem, their heart shall turn again unto their lord Rehoboam, and they shall kill me.
precepts.point: Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared that if the people kept going up to sacrifice at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, their heart would turn again unto Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him; so he took counsel and made two calves of gold with his own hands, doubling the iniquity of the wilderness, and said, behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why: The first thing the children of Dan did in the land was set up the graven image, and Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared: “If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, even unto Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me”. That fear is what drove him to make gods for the people, and Dan, the tribe that had kept Micah’s graven image with its own priests all the time the house of God was in Shiloh, is where one of them went.

precepts.point: Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day, a feast he devised of his own heart, and offered on the altar at Bethel sacrificing to the calves he made. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today, and after forty years of peace under Solomon the nation of Israel began to decline even more.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

precepts.why:
“It was also contained in the same writing, that the prophet, being warned of God, commanded the tabernacle and the ark to go with him, as he went forth into the mountain, where Moses climbed up, and saw the heritage of God.” There Jeremy “found an hollow cave, wherein he laid the tabernacle, and the ark, and the altar of incense, and so stopped the door.” Those who followed “could not find it”, and he said, “As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that God gather his people again together, and receive them unto mercy.”

Jeremiah hid the ark in a cave, and it is lost until the Most High gathers his people. So it is not in Ethiopia, and no man has it.

Jeroboam turned Israel away from the house of the Lord at Jerusalem. He said, “It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt”, set golden calves in Bethel and Dan, made priests “of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi”, and ordained a feast “in the month which he had devised of his own heart”. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today. After forty years of peace under Solomon, the nation of Israel began to decline even more.

precepts.text: Jeroboam made two calves of gold and set them in Bethel and in Dan, telling Israel these were the gods that brought them out of Egypt, and this thing became a sin.
precepts.point: Nevertheless he cleaves to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, and departs not from them. The house of Ahab had reared up images and led the kingdom into idolatry.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

precepts.why:
Jehoram “cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin”. Here is that sin. Jeroboam “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” He set one in Bethel and the other in Dan, “And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.”

Jehoram the son of Ahab wrought evil, “but not like his father, and like his mother: for he put away the image of Baal that his father had made.” He put away Baal, but not the calves. The house of Ahab had reared up images and led the kingdom into idolatry, and even the son who took down Baal “departed not therefrom”: he held on to Jeroboam’s golden calves, the sin that made Israel to sin.

precepts.text: Jeroboam makes two calves of gold and tells Israel these are their gods, driving out true worship and forcing the faithful to seek the Lord in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Those out of all the tribes who set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel come to Jerusalem to sacrifice, and for three years they strengthen the kingdom of Judah and walk in the way of David and Solomon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

precepts.why:
“Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” He set one in Beth-el and the other in Dan, “And this thing became a sin.”

That is why the Levites left. Jeroboam “ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made”, and cast Levi off from executing the priest's office unto the Lord. So Levi had to return where they could serve: “the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem.”

The calves drove out true worship and forced the faithful to seek the Lord in Jerusalem. Out of all the tribes, “such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem”, and for three years they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and “walked in the way of David and Solomon.”

precepts.text: Israel departed from Rehoboam, splitting into the northern and southern kingdoms.
precepts.point: Isaiah is a heavy, prophetic book; even the Ethiopian eunuch was reading Isaiah when the spirit sent Philip to help him understand it.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

precepts.why:
The friction between Rehoboam and Jeroboam finished what Solomon’s idolatry began. “So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.”

Israel departed from Rehoboam, splitting into the northern and southern kingdoms. That is why Isaiah’s vision is “concerning Judah and Jerusalem” under the kings of Judah: the kingdom was already divided.

precepts.text: Israel says, "What portion have we in David?" and departs to their tents, and only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.
precepts.point: The division began when Rehoboam refused the people and Jeroboam led the ten tribes away, so the southern kingdom (Judah, Benjamin, Levi) and the northern kingdom went their separate ways, and the Levites and a remnant that set their hearts to seek the Most High left the north and came to Judah. This is the same enmity you keep seeing as Jew and Gentile in the New Testament.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Peter says, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation.” “One of another nation” is not other races. It is the northern kingdom, and this whole verse rests on the split between Judah and Ephraim.

The division began when Rehoboam refused the people: “the king hearkened not unto the people; for the cause was from the Lord.” Then Israel answered, “What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” They stoned Adoram, made Jeroboam king over all Israel, “there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.”

“So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.” That is where the enmity begins that you keep seeing as Jew and Gentile in the New Testament.

precepts.text: Shemaiah the man of God tells Rehoboam and Judah not to fight their brethren the children of Israel, for the division was from the Most High.
precepts.point: The division began when Rehoboam refused the people and Jeroboam led the ten tribes away, so the southern kingdom (Judah, Benjamin, Levi) and the northern kingdom went their separate ways, and the Levites and a remnant that set their hearts to seek the Most High left the north and came to Judah. This is the same enmity you keep seeing as Jew and Gentile in the New Testament.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Rehoboam gathered “all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men” to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back. But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God: “Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me.”

The division was from the Most High. The southern kingdom, Judah and Benjamin, and the northern kingdom went their separate ways, and they were still brethren, “your brethren the children of Israel.” The one of “another nation” in Peter's mouth is that brother, the northern kingdom.

precepts.text: Jeroboam sets golden calves in Bethel and Dan, saying, "Behold thy gods, O Israel," and devises a feast in the eighth month out of his own heart.
precepts.point: Jeroboam sealed the split with idolatry, making two golden calves in Bethel and Dan, ordaining a feast of his own in the eighth month, and setting up priests of the lowest people, so the northern kingdom sank deeper and deeper into idol worship. Dan fell so hard that the tribe was absorbed and left out of the sealed tribes.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Jeroboam sealed the split with idolatry. He “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” He set one in Bethel and the other in Dan, “And this thing became a sin.”

He “made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi. And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah.” A feast of his own, out of his own heart.

From there the northern kingdom sank deeper and deeper into idol worship. That idolatry is why Judah would not keep company with them.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
How the northern kingdom became strangers from the covenants: Jeroboam “said in his heart, Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David: If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, even unto Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me.” So he “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan.”

The northern kingdom was excommunicated because Jeroboam prohibited them from going to Jerusalem to sacrifice. Cut off from the sacrifice, they could never be saved under a covenant that required animal sacrifice, which is why the false brethren's doctrine would have shut them out.

points: Jeroboam said in his heart, if this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, and they shall kill me. So the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said, behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. He set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: And this thing became a sin unto the northern kingdom, because all the kings after that who did the same were compared back to Jeroboam.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: Rehoboam refused the elders' counsel to lighten the tax Solomon laid on the people to build shrines for his wives. He promised scorpions instead of whips.
Israel answered, what portion have we in David? They stoned the tax collector and made Jeroboam king, and God forbade Judah to fight them because the split was from him.

Jeroboam feared the people would return to Rehoboam if they worshipped at Jerusalem. He set golden calves in Bethel and Dan, made priests of the lowest people instead of Levites, and invented his own feast in the eighth month.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to make him king. Jeroboam, still in Egypt, heard of it and returned, and the congregation of Israel came to Rehoboam asking him to lighten the grievous yoke and heavy service his father had put on them.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: The heavy yoke was the labor of the building; Solomon did not enslave his own people as he did the other nations, but they did have to put in that work. Rehoboam told them to depart three days and return, which was wisdom, for it is right to take time and get counsel before giving an answer.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with.

Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: The young men told him to say his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, and that where his father chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions, which was disrespectful.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: The king hearkened not to the people, for the cause was from the Most High, that he might perform the saying he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam; the prophecy had to come to pass.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: When all Israel saw the king would not hearken, they said, What portion have we in David? To your tents, O Israel. So Israel departed and rebelled against the house of David to this day, and only over those in the cities of Judah did Rehoboam reign.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Rehoboam sent Adoram who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, so the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. This is the split, the northern tribes rebelling against the house of David until this day.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: When Israel heard Jeroboam had returned, they called him to the congregation and made him king over Israel; none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only. That is how Jeroboam got the ten tribes.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah with Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: But the word of the Most High came to Shemaiah the man of God, telling Rehoboam and the house of Judah and Benjamin not to fight against their brethren the children of Israel, for this thing was from the Most High; and they hearkened and returned home.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and Penuel, and feared in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice at Jerusalem their hearts would turn again to Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Jeroboam took counsel and made two calves of gold, telling Israel it was too much to go up to Jerusalem, and setting one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, and this thing became a sin. He made a house of high places and priests of the lowest of the people, not of the sons of Levi.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day, a feast he devised of his own heart, and offered on the altar at Bethel sacrificing to the calves he made. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today, and after forty years of peace under Solomon the nation of Israel began to decline even more.
